chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said:
There is no ritual more beloved to Allah than the Sa'ee, and that is because therein every tyrant is humbled.

key_terms.السَّعْيِ: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.الْجَبَّارِينَ: The tyrants or those who are arrogant and overbearing

ai.seo_question: Why is the Sa'ee considered the most beloved ritual to Allah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith emphasizes the metaphysical impact of Sa'ee by noting that Allah finds no ritual more beloved than this act of humble movement. It uniquely interprets the physical exertion as a means of subduing 'al-jabbarin' (the tyrants or arrogant ones), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that ritual acts possess both internal spiritual purification and external cosmic significance. This perspective aligns with the concept of 'tazkiyah' (purification) through bodily submission, reinforcing the ritual's role in overcoming spiritual arrogance.
